newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala to invite bids for railway concessions.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala to invite bids for railway concessions.

text.p: The Guatemalan Railroad Company (Fegua) planned to announce next week the invitations to bid for railway concessions, but the bidding rules would not be published until mid-February, an official said Friday.
"On Monday we will announce the invitation for bids. Beginning February 17 people can pick up the bidding terms," Fegua auditor Andres Porras told Reuters.
In its first privatization a state-owned company, Guatemala will seek investors to rehabilitate and operate the decaying, abandoned state-owned railway.

Porras said potential bidders will have to pay a $1,000 fee for the bidding terms and the state would receive bids over a three month period, opening them on May 15. During the bid period companies can study the state of the railway.
In September, Price Waterhouse appraised at $35 million Fegua's assets, including 60,000 tons of 100-year-old rails, 30 diesel locomotives and 1,180 rail cars.
The assets do not include real estate or rights of way, which will be retained by the state.
The railroad of rotting ties and outdated equipment has fallen completely out of use in recent years and is a money drain for the government, losing approximately $33,000 a year.
Competing companies will be granted concessions to rehabilitate and use the rails and railroad stations and the state will receive a small percentage of railway income.
